title: The first confirmed alien planets orbit a dead star
body: In 1992 astronomers Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail confirmed planets around PSR B1257+12, a pulsar about 2,300 light-years away. A pulsar is the spinning, collapsed core left behind when a massive star explodes. They found the planets through tiny, regular shifts in the timing of its radio pulses, which arrive about 161 times a second. The first planet around a Sun-like star wasn’t found until 1995, and pulsar planets turned out to be rare.

slides.question: How were the planets around the pulsar PSR B1257+12 found?
options: Direct photos from a space telescope
Tiny shifts in the timing of its pulses
Wobbles seen in its visible light
